subject: Next steps: SDK launchpad (Python/TS) - env, samples, local smoke tests
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@sparkhealth.ai>, Emily Baker <emily@devops.sparkhealth.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, May 2, 2028 at 3:12 PM -0700
Subject: Next steps: SDK launchpad (Python/TS) - env, samples, local smoke tests

Alex / Emily - thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so your team can start a fast local validation of Redwood SDKs (Python + TypeScript) and our sample apps. Please reply with any constraints and the best dev contact to loop in for the sandbox.

TL;DR next actions (what we'll deliver / what we need from you):
- Redwood: provide sample repo (Python + TS), a short integration checklist, ephemeral sandbox API key, and a small smoke test script for generation + embeddings/reranking. Attachments: integration-checklist.pdf, redwood-sdk-sample-arch.png
- SparkHealth: confirm local environment (OS + Python/Node versions), whether outbound egress is allowed to api.redwood.ai or if you need a proxy/VPN, and the developer who will run the tests.

Minimum environment we expect for the local smoke run:
- macOS/Linux or Windows WSL2; Docker optional but recommended for reproducibility.
- Python 3.10+ (venv), pip install -r requirements.txt (we use requests + redwood SDK sham)
- Node 18.x (Yarn or npm) for the TS sample; we provide a small express sample to show streaming + tool-calling stub.
- Network: outbound HTTPS to api.redwood.ai:443; if you block egress we'll provide alternate proxy instructions.

Quick sample steps (full repo link in Drive):
1) Clone: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-launchpad 
2) Python smoke: cd sdk-launchpad/python-samples && python -m venv .env && source .env/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && REDWOOD_API_KEY=<{ephemeral_key}> python smoke_generate.py
3) TS smoke: cd ../ts-samples && npm install && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=<{ephemeral_key}> && npm run smoke

Embedding / reranker check: smoke_generate includes a short embed -> nearest-neighbor rerank flow; smoke_rerank.py will return a small similarity table so you can compare against an internal baseline.

Security / compliance: I've attached the integration checklist with the minimal items your security team typically asks for (network, logging, data retention). If you need SOC2 artifacts we can route that via our security team after the initial tech validation.

Proposed times for a short 30-minute tech pairing (we'll walk through local run and proxy env):
- Mon May 6: 10:00-10:30 PT
- Tue May 7: 13:00-13:30 PT

Please confirm which slot works and who from SparkHealth will be running the tests.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive - Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

Attachment stubs: integration-checklist.pdf (6 pages), redwood-sdk-sample-arch.png (PNG image)

From: Alex Nguyen <alex@sparkhealth.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Baker <emily@devops.sparkhealth.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, May 2, 2028 at 4:05 PM -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: SDK launchpad (Python/TS) - env, samples, local smoke tests

Thanks Karthik - useful summary. A few notes from our side before the pairing: 

- Environment: primary environment is Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (devs use macOS as well). We're on Python 3.10 in CI and Node 18 for front-end tooling. That should be fine.
- Network: SparkHealth is on-prem-first. Egress is tightly controlled - we cannot make direct outbound calls to external APIs from our production network. Our dev machines (non-prod VLAN) can do outbound HTTPS but only via a corporate proxy (proxy.sparkhealth.internal:3128). If your samples can support standard HTTP(S) proxy env vars (HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY) that should be enough for the smoke tests.
- Security docs: Emily (cc'd) will lead the security review. Please include a short list of logging/data retention behaviors for the smoke run and a pointer to SOC2 evidence. We’ll initiate our internal security intake once we have the checklist.

We can do the pairing on Mon May 6 at 10:00 PT - that works for our lead engineer (Emily) and me. Can you confirm an invite? Also, please send the ephemeral key and sandbox URL via a secure channel (we prefer a separate email for credentials).

On Thu, May 2, 2028 at 3:12 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex / Emily - thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so your team can start a fast local validation of Redwood SDKs (Python + TypeScript) and our sample apps. Please reply with any constraints and the best dev contact to loop in for the sandbox.

Best,
Alex Nguyen
Director of Engineering | SparkHealth
alex@sparkhealth.ai | +1 617-555-0133

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@sparkhealth.ai>, Emily Baker <emily@devops.sparkhealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, May 3, 2028 at 9:20 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: SDK launchpad (Python/TS) - env, samples, local smoke tests

Alex / Emily - Neha from the developer success team here. Thanks for the details - we can absolutely support standard HTTP(S) proxy environment variables and will provide explicit instructions in the repo README.

What I'm provisioning for you ahead of Monday's pairing:
- Ephemeral sandbox API key (will send in a separate email to Alex only) - scope: generative + embeddings, 48-hour expiry.
- Sandbox host: https://sandbox-us.redwood.ai/sh-sandbox-0427 (whitelistable).
- Developer sandbox user: emily.dev@sparkhealth.internal (we'll create a token that maps to that username for audit logs).
- Attached: integration-checklist.pdf - I've highlighted the rows relevant to local dev runs (network, proxy, token rotation, data retention).

Quick proxy examples you can try in the smoke scripts if your dev machines use the corporate proxy:
- Linux / macOS (bash): export HTTPS_PROXY=https://proxy.sparkhealth.internal:3128
- Node (TS sample): run with HTTPS_PROXY set, or in code use: 
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, proxy: process.env.HTTPS_PROXY });
- Python: requests honors HTTPS_PROXY env var; smoke_generate.py includes a check and prints a helpful error if the proxy blocks TLS.

Local smoke snippets (included in the repo README):
- cURL quick generation test:
  curl -sS -X POST https://sandbox-us.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-mini-1","prompt":"Hello from SparkHealth"}'

- Python (requests):
  import os
  import requests
  r = requests.post('https://sandbox-us.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', headers={'Authorization': f"Bearer {os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')}"}, json={'input':['a','b']})
  print(r.json())

- TS: npm run smoke will run a small script that posts a generation, then an embeddings call, then a local rerank using cosine similarity (results printed to stdout).

We’ll send the ephemeral key to Alex in a separate secure email and create a calendar invite for Mon May 6 10:00 PT with a short pairing agenda (install + smoke run + proxy troubleshooting). Looking forward to it.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Developer Success - Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Thanks - see you Monday at 10:00 PT.
